name: Johanan
overview: Johanan was a male Benjamite who played a supportive role in the life of David by coming to his aid at Ziklag. His presence is noted specifically in the context of David's time at Ziklag, marking him as a loyal ally during a critical period. As a member of the tribe of Benjamin, Johanan's involvement highlights the unity among the tribes in supporting David.
namesAndTitles: The name Johanan means "YHWH is gracious," reflecting a theologically rich meaning tied to God's gracious character. This proper name is mentioned explicitly in 1 Chronicles 12:4 and does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Johanan as a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, establishing his tribal identity clearly. Beyond this lineage, no additional family relationships are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Johanan's significance lies in his allegiance to David during a formative time when David was gathering support at Ziklag. His coming to David's aid represents the growing recognition and acceptance of David's leadership among the Benjamites. This support was crucial in consolidating David's position as a future king in Israel.
